query: High-entropy alloys contain five or more elements at 5–35 at% each, generally with comparable atomic radii. Refractory and nickel-based high-entropy alloys have demonstrated elevated-temperature mechanical properties comparable to titanium- and nickel-based alloys used in extreme environments because of their heat resistance and specific strength. However, prior investigations have mainly treated titanium and nickel as additions, leaving alloys in which both are primary constituents unexplored. Subject to the stated compositional definition, what single testable intervention hypothesis could improve the elevated-temperature mechanical properties of a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy relative to the same material without the intervention? Specify the intervention, causal mechanism, predicted relative outcome, composition and operating boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding 3–5 at% tungsten to a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy, coupled with an appropriate homogenization heat treatment, will improve elevated-temperature mechanical properties by forming fine, thermally stable tungsten-enriched intermetallic precipitates that inhibit grain-boundary sliding and dislocation motion.
generation.material_initial_state: A high-entropy alloy where titanium and nickel are the primary constituents with other elements present at 5–35 at% each, but without tungsten.
generation.intervention: Introduce tungsten at 3–5 at% into the alloy composition and apply a homogenization heat treatment designed to promote uniform dispersal and controlled precipitation of tungsten-rich phases.
generation.conditions: Mechanical testing conducted at elevated temperatures (approximately 700–900°C) under conditions simulating high-temperature service (e.g., creep and tensile loading).
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of fine, tungsten-enriched intermetallic precipitates along grain boundaries.
generation.mechanism: Tungsten, a refractory element, can segregate to grain boundaries during heat treatment, forming precipitates that stabilize the microstructure and hinder dislocation movement and grain-boundary sliding at high temperatures, thereby enhancing strength and creep resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the baseline alloy without tungsten, the tungsten-doped alloy should exhibit an improvement in elevated-temperature yield strength and creep resistance, with an expected performance increase on the order of approximately 15–20% under the specified testing conditions.
generation.baseline: The titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy without tungsten addition.
generation.boundary: The predicted enhancement is expected only within the tungsten addition range of 3–5 at% and for operating temperatures between 700°C and 900°C; effects outside these ranges are not established.
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of the performance improvement and the stability of the tungsten-enriched precipitates at the extremes of the testing range remain uncertain without experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sample sets: one set of the base titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy and one set with an additional 3–5 at% tungsten. Subject both sets to an identical homogenization heat treatment and then conduct mechanical testing (tensile strength, creep rate measurements) at 700°C, 800°C, and 900°C. Complement the mechanical tests with microstructural analyses (e.g., TEM or SEM) to confirm the formation of tungsten-enriched precipitates.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the tungsten-doped samples do not exhibit a statistically significant improvement (at least a 15% increase in yield strength or a corresponding reduction in creep rate) compared to the baseline, or if the microstructural analysis fails to show the formation of tungsten-enriched precipitates, then the hypothesis is falsified.

chosen.approach: Alloy intervention via element additions, processing, heat treatments or coatings
